title: Secrets Management & Azure Key Vault in .NET
description: Eliminate hardcoded API credentials using Azure Key Vault, Managed Identity, .NET User Secrets, and automated secret rotation.

data.text: The Zero-Secret Architecture for AI Applications

Hardcoded API keys and database credentials committed to Git repositories remain one of the most common causes of enterprise security breaches. In generative AI engineering, where commercial API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Azure) grant unrestricted access to metered cloud compute, an exposed secret can incur tens of thousands of dollars in unauthorized usage within hours. Modern .NET architectures enforce a zero-secret rule: credentials are never stored in source control, configuration files, or container image layers.

rows: Stored outside project directory in user profile (%APPDATA% / ~/.microsoft)
Short-lived cryptographic tokens without permanent passwords
Zero stored Azure service principal secrets
DefaultAzureCredential reading secrets from Key Vault over Private Endpoints
Hardware Security Module (HSM) encryption, automated audit logging, access policies

data.text: Integrating Azure Key Vault with ASP.NET Core Configuration
By adding the Azure Key Vault configuration provider, secrets stored in Key Vault seamlessly overlay into IConfiguration alongside appsettings.json, enabling seamless dependency injection.

data.text: During local development, use the .NET Secret Manager tool to store API keys outside of the project tree:

data.title: Using dotnet user-secrets CLI
data.content: Initializes and stores local development keys:
data.code:
# 1. Initialize user secrets for the project
dotnet user-secrets init --project src/LearnAI.Api

# 2. Store local OpenAI API key safely
dotnet user-secrets set "OpenAI:ApiKey" "sk-local-dev-key-12345" --project src/LearnAI.Api

# 3. List stored secrets
dotnet user-secrets list --project src/LearnAI.Api

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Never commit API keys or connection strings to Git: enforce pre-commit secret scanners
Use .NET Secret Manager (dotnet user-secrets) for local developer workstations
Deploy Azure Key Vault in production and authenticate via DefaultAzureCredential Managed Identity
Configure automatic Key Vault reload intervals to handle zero-downtime secret rotations
Favor native Managed Identity over API keys whenever communicating with Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search
data.takeaway: Secrets management is an enterprise prerequisite. Combining .NET User Secrets locally with Azure Key Vault in production enforces a strict zero-secret posture across the application lifecycle.
